newsitem.title: USA: MCI says largest stakeholder in Pan Am Cable.
newsitem.headline: MCI says largest stakeholder in Pan Am Cable.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp. said Wednesday that it is the largest U.S. stockholder of the new $214 million Pan American Cable System connecting the United States with Central and South America.
The Washington-based company said it owns more than a 10 percent stake in the cable, which will be 4,354 miles long, is expected to go into service in mid-1998.
A company spokesman declined to give a dollar figure on MCI's contribution.
The cable will run from the U.S. Virgin Islands to Aruba, Venezuela, Colombia, Panama, Ecuador, Peru, and Chile.
Other investors in the cable are Telefonica del Peru SA, Telecom Italia, Emetel Ecuador, CANTV of Venezuela, Telecom Colombia and MCII de Venezuela.
The cable will allow MCI to provide broadband switched services and broadband access to such services as the Internet, MCI said.
